opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ordinarily resident in Scotland, enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish institution, and not eligible for government funding for their tuition fees. Must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain, or be an asylum seeker.
opportunities.summary: Covers tuition fees for students from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government, enrolled on an undergraduate degree at a Scottish higher education institution. Also supports eligible second-degree students reskilling in skills-shortage areas.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh), studying full-time or part-time. Must be ordinarily resident in Scotland, entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, and not have already obtained a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A partnership between Carnegie Education Fund and Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh providing funding for Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households to undertake postgraduate study (SCQF Level 11) in plant science and botany, covering full tuition fees and a living-cost bursary.
